note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: KV cache growth in LRMs and the failure of recent-query scoring, via the TRT observation and clustered global queries, motivate BeaconKV and its results

nodes.name: KV cache bottleneck in LRMs
nodes.description: Long CoT reasoning makes the KV cache grow linearly with sequence length; e.g. Qwen3-4B generating 32K tokens at batch size 16 needs over 77GB of KV cache, near the limit of an 80GB GPU.

nodes.name: Recent-query scoring assumption
nodes.description: Existing KV compression methods (e.g. RPC, R-KV) score KV importance with attention from recent queries, assuming they are reliable proxies for future attention.

nodes.name: Thought Revisiting Tokens exist
nodes.description: In LRM decoding, global queries attend to distant keys (e.g. early task-solving plans and problem constraints) rather than nearby ones; the corresponding tokens are called Thought Revisiting Tokens (TRT), and their attention distances are clearly separated from those of local queries.

nodes.name: TRT occur sporadically across heads
nodes.description: Global queries appear with varying frequency across many layers and heads and occur sporadically and unpredictably in the reasoning trace.

nodes.name: Recent queries miss TRT
nodes.description: Because TRT are sporadic, recent-query-based methods cannot anticipate which distant KV pairs future TRT will revisit, causing premature eviction of essential KV pairs and degraded reasoning under tight budgets.

nodes.name: Global queries cluster
nodes.description: Global queries have low similarity to neighbouring local queries but high mutual similarity, and cluster into a small number of similarity groups in the query embedding space (PCA, Fig 4).

nodes.name: Beacon queries represent clusters
nodes.description: A compact set of beacon queries, one representative per global query cluster, can anticipate which KV pairs future global queries will revisit without storing the entire query history.

nodes.name: BeaconKV observation set
nodes.description: BeaconKV, a training-free method, scores KV pairs using observation queries made of recent queries plus beacon queries selected by Continual Farthest Point Sampling (FPS), a bounded-buffer online algorithm.

nodes.name: Max-aggregation scoring
nodes.description: BeaconKV aggregates attention over observation queries by max-pooling rather than mean-pooling, since TRT signals are high-magnitude but rare and mean-pooling would dilute them.

nodes.name: Higher accuracy than RPC and R-KV
nodes.description: On R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-14B across AIME24, MATH-500, LiveCodeBench and GPQA-Diamond, BeaconKV generally outperforms RPC and R-KV, with gains up to 31.7 points (Qwen3-14B, AIME24, budget 1024).

nodes.name: Memory and throughput gains
nodes.description: On Qwen3-4B with 32K generation on an A100 80GB, BeaconKV with a 2K budget cuts peak memory from 77.0GB to 13.3GB (5.8x) and raises throughput from 82.3 to 356.4 tokens/s (over 4.3x).

nodes.name: Same efficiency as RPC, better accuracy
nodes.description: At matched 2K and 1K budgets BeaconKV matches RPC's throughput and memory while improving LiveCodeBench accuracy by +6.3 and +12.3 points.

nodes.name: Balanced query split is best
nodes.description: A balanced (16 recent, 16 beacon) observation set gives 64.6% accuracy at 4355.7s latency, while over-allocating to beacons (1,31) gives 63.5% at 10871.3s.

nodes.name: Max beats mean aggregation
nodes.description: Max aggregation generally outperforms mean aggregation, e.g. 23.3 vs 18.8 at a 256-token budget (Table 2).

nodes.name: Gains not from initial queries alone
nodes.description: BeaconKV consistently outperforms an Initial+Recent baseline, indicating gains come from Continual FPS dynamically capturing evolving global query patterns, not merely preserving early context.

structural_reasoning: Problem (KV memory), diagnosis (recent queries miss TRT; global queries cluster), method (beacon queries, Continual FPS, max pooling), then results and ablations.
